tables.head: Seljuk
rows: Founder
Tughril Beg
Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi
Salahuddin (Saladin)
Shah Ismail I
Period
1171 to 1250 (Egypt)
Achievement
Won the battle of Manzikert against the Byzantines (1071) and united Persia, Iraq and Anatolia under Sunni rule
Founded the city of Cairo (969) and ruled Egypt, North Africa and Syria
Defeated the Crusaders at Hattin and took back Jerusalem (1187)
United Persia and made it a strong state with Twelver Shia Islam as its religion
Contributions 1)- 2)-
1) Nizamiyya madrasas built by Nizam-ul-Mulk 2) the Jalali calendar and an observatory under Malik Shah
1) Al-Azhar mosque and university 2) the library and House of Knowledge in Cairo
1) the Citadel of Cairo 2) madrasas and hospitals
1) the buildings of Isfahan (Naqsh-e Jahan Square, Shah Mosque) 2) Persian carpets and miniature painting
Causes of decline 1)- 2)-
1) quarrels among Seljuk princes 2) the rise of the Khwarazmian shahs and Mongol attacks
1) weak caliphs ruled by powerful viziers 2) the Crusades; Saladin ended the dynasty in 1171
1) quarrels among the heirs of Saladin 2) the Mamluks took power in 1250
1) weak shahs and loss of military strength 2) the Afghan invasion (1722) and trade monopolies

tables.head: Policy
rows: Financial
Raja Todar Mal's land revenue system: land was measured and the tax fixed in cash from the average harvest; the jizya was abolished
Kept the land revenue system, re-imposed the jizya (1679) and gave up some old cesses; long wars emptied the treasury
Religious
Tolerance for all faiths (Sulh-e-Kul): the Ibadat Khana for religious talks; no tax on pilgrims
Followed the Sharia strictly: ended music at court and compiled the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri
Administrative
Mansabdari system: every officer had a rank (mansab); the empire was divided into subas, sarkars and parganas
Kept the same system, but there were too many mansabdars and too few jagirs, and the long wars in the Deccan stretched the administration
